findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there to be multiple food items out of cold holding temperatures in the bottom of the prep cooler closest to the dish area. Probed temperature of cut watermelon 46 degree F, Probed temperature of brisket 50 degrees F, ambient temperature on the internal thermometer of the cooler 50 degree F. These food items had recently been placed in this cooler from the walk in cooler. All items in this cooler were moved to the other cooler on the cook line. Ensure that all cold holding equipment keeps food items at or below 41 degrees Fahrenheit. Follow up has been scheduled for Tuesday, September 29, 2026 to ensure that cooler is keeping food at or below 41 degrees Fahrenheit.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of ice on the floor and ceiling of the walk in freezer. The PIC mentioned a work order will be placed to address this issue. Ensure that the walk in freezer is maintained and free of ice accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container of raw beef stored above cooked seafood in a prep cooler along the cookline. The items were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal proteins are never stored above any ready-to-eat (RTE) foods to protect against cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: All sanitizer solutions throughout the restaurants were testing less than 100ppm (quat). These included sanitizer from the main triple sink and all buckets stored along the cookline. The sanitizer bag connected to the sink dispenser was observed empty. The bag was replaced by the PIC and retested at 200ppm to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentrations to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector probed heavy cream in the beverage cooler of the facility. Heavy cream probed at 50F. It and another carton of half and half were discarded immediately by the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are always kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the beverage cooler to not be holding food at 41F or below. See violation 22 for foods. Inspector originally observed the cooler holding food at ~50F. Inspector watched PIC discard food, and then had the cooler closed and left until the end of the inspection. At the end of the inspection, the cooler was holding ~49F. Ensure cooler is serviced so that it holds food at or below 41F.

Inspector will return 10/09/2025 to re-inspect cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Inspector observed sanitation bucket to contain little to no quat. Dispenser above three part sink was tested and was shown to not dispense quat in an acceptable concentration. PIC replaced sanitizer supply bag, fixing the concentration issue. Quat tested at 200ppm after switch. Ensure quat dispenser and sani-buckets are tested every day to maintain proper concentrations of sanitizer.

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP
findings.comment:
8-201.13: Inspector observed vacuum-sealing taking place at establishment, but establishment has no HACCP for vacuum sealing. Education was given on the possible safety hazards associated with vacuum sealing. Colleen will follow up with the establishment to help formulate a HACCP plan.

(A) Before engaging in activity requiring HACCP, PERMIT HOLDER must have approval.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Anti-slip floor in the doorway of the dry storage area was observed to be peeling up.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure floor is repaired to obtain a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice bin was observed to contain mold on sides of bin.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on site.  Ensure ice bin is cleaned regularly to prevent mold growth and ice contamination.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
A temperature measuring device is not present at facility.  Discussed with PIC, provided information on how to obtain temperature measuring disk.  Ensure a temperature measuring device is provided and readily accessible.

4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Mop basin and dish machine was observed to need caulked to the wall.  Discussed with PIC, facility maintenance department will be contacted to caulk areas.  Ensure areas are smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans in walk-in cooler (non-dairy). Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed buildup of dust on fans in walk-in cooler. Ensure these places are cleaned frequently to prevent contamination of food in walk-in.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) QAC sanitizer at 0 ppm at sanitation bucket. Provide 200ppm. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. Provide a freeze date and a thaw date on the labels.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
(A) Heavy Cream in Line Kitchen small prep cooler found opened, and without date marking.  Director states that had students properly cleaned up work station, cream would have been returned to walk-in cooler for later use.  CORRECTED - cream was immediately labeled with date of opening.  
(B) Cooler at Instructor Station in main lab kitchen (in the middle of horseshoe) had heavy cream dated 1/22 and milk dated 1/27.  CORRECTED - both items were immediately, voluntarily discarded.
In this kitchen, in which many cooks and students come and go, make sure all ready-to-eat, potentially hazardous foods are marked with date of opening, and used or discarded in 7 days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Several scoops in bakery kitchen were found fallen down into flour (in white rolling bins).  CORRECTED - scoops were righted so their handles were extended out of food.  Make sure all students and staff take caution to always store scoop with handle up.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Ice paddles are stored on the lower shelf of the walk-in freezer with open shelving above (REPEAT).  Store ice paddles so food-contact, sanitized surfaces are protected (i.e. in sealed tubs, by plastic wrap, deli paper, etc.).
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.     750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Mop was found damp, bunched up in bottom of mop sink.  CORRECTED - mop was draped to facilitate drying.  Anytime mop is not in use, it should be hung in a way that facilitates drying and eliminates providing water and harborage for potential pests.  Also, mop water should always be immediately discarded after use.
750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.
